A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ASIDE, with identifiable corresponding methods, experiments, and analyses. All 18 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning, separation, utility, and prompt-injection results in Tables 1–4, together with representation analyses and rotation ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original separation, utility, and safety evaluations, including BIPIA results, embedding interventions, and additional representation analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: V1 doubles the embedding matrix, initializes the data copy with a rotation, and learns both copies independently. V2 instead shares one embedding matrix and applies a fixed, nonlearnable rotation to data embeddings during each forward pass. This substantially changes parameter sharing and inference while eliminating additional embedding parameters.

E1.justification: V2 adds BIPIA evaluations covering malicious instructions embedded in Email QA, Web QA, Table QA, summarization, and Code QA contexts. This substantially broadens indirect-injection task coverage. The Alpaca training data, SEP, AlpacaEval, Structured Query, and four direct-injection benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: ASIDE-Copy is removed, and the downstream representation comparison in Section 6.4 switches from ASIDE-Copy to Vanilla. Main benchmark comparator sets otherwise remain the same; SFT is renamed Vanilla, and extending those comparators to additional models and BIPIA does not introduce another defense method.

E3.justification: The reported training protocol changes from fixed learning rate, batch size, and warm-up settings to validation-selected grids spanning learning rates, batch sizes, and warm-up ratios. V2 also evaluates Qwen2.5 7B and Mistral 7B v0.3, restricts BIPIA to programmatically evaluable attacks, and introduces paired embedding-intervention procedures. These substantially revise the experimental design.

E4.justification: V2 adds interventions testing whether rerouting injection tokens makes them executable, separates probe-token feature activations, analyzes successful versus unsuccessful injections, and adds Llama 2 analysis panels. Conversely, v1's ASIDE-Copy initialization ablation, embedding-drift measurements, and Appendix E rotation-angle sweep are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors for SEP, direct-attack means and standard deviations over three random seeds, and standard-deviation shading for representation similarities. Additional result rows and plots do not establish a changed statistical procedure or increased repeated-run count.

E6.justification: Many retained results are replaced: Llama 3.1 8B ASIDE's SEP is 88.6% in v1 Table 1 versus 83.1% in v2 Table 3; TensorTrust ASR is 53.1% versus 36.6% in the corresponding safety tables. Architecture and training changed, so these are not matched-setting performance gains or losses. V2 also adds substantial benchmark and intervention results while removing ablation results.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1 Section 3.2's attention-score equation and argument that orthogonal embedding rotation preserves within-role attention scores. Appendix A retains the isoclinic-rotation definition and block-diagonal construction. This is a localized removal of mathematical reasoning rather than a new theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine the contribution around a fixed transformation without additional parameters, replacing v1's separately learned role-specific embeddings. The introduction also extends the claimed empirical scope to Qwen and Mistral. Improved separation and safety without dedicated safety training remain central claims.

C2.justification: V1's initialization and local-minimum explanation gives way to low-rank-subspace motivation and an interpretation of rotation as a noisy control over executability. V2 newly attributes Mistral's SEP Utility difference, 45.0% for Vanilla versus 25.3% for ASIDE, to brittle evaluation. Discussion of alternative architectures and complementary defenses is also substantially revised.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces single-configuration reporting with explicit search grids, batch/accumulation pairs, and an effective-batch calculation; Appendix F adds concrete attack prompts. Some checkpointing and save/evaluation details disappear, and selected per-model configurations are not listed. Hardware, libraries, and data-access links remain, making this a limited revision of existing reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to classify defenses and discuss SecAlign, injection detection, circuit breakers, CaMeL, prefix tuning, rotary embeddings, and low-rank representations. Positioning against ISE changes from emphasizing flexible per-token embeddings to emphasizing parameter-free rotation and stronger separation in deeper layers.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method, results discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Method subsections become architectural/training paragraphs, Structured Query descriptions move to Appendix F, and SFT becomes Vanilla. These changes substantially reshape the narrative beyond merely inserting new experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, the main separation table becomes Figure 2 with detailed numbers in Appendix Table 3, and safety results are consolidated into an expanded summary table. New intervention and conditional-feature plots are added, histograms distinguish probe tokens, and the initialization table and angle-sweep figure disappear.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the paper through a simpler parameter-free formulation, broader model/task validation, and interventions that test the proposed mechanism. These gains are tempered by removed rotation ablations and numerical inconsistencies: for Llama 2 13B ASIDE, Table 1 reports 31.4% StruQ-ID ASR, whereas Table 4's 62.6% robust accuracy implies 37.4% ASR. The Mistral utility loss also qualifies the retained utility-preservation claim, limiting the net quality improvement.
